record.question:
After a developer accidentally terminates a production EC2 instance, a company reviews its developer roles and finds overlapping administrative policies. Only a designated architect role should be able to stop or terminate production instances. Instances carry a protected Environment=Production tag. The company wants both an explicit preventive restriction and least-privilege developer permissions.

Which actions should the solutions architect take? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Explicitly deny StopInstances and TerminateInstances for developer roles when the target carries the production tag. Prevent developers from changing that tag or altering or bypassing the restriction.

Remove broad developer permissions and privilege-escalation paths, including overlapping policies and access to the architect role. Grant production stop and terminate permissions only to the designated architect role.
Require developers to use MFA when calling StopInstances or TerminateInstances, while retaining their production permissions.
Remove developer workstation addresses from the production instances' security groups, while retaining their EC2 API permissions.
Replace the developers' administrative policies with the AWS managed PowerUserAccess policy as the sole permission change.

explanation.text:
<<1>> and <<2>> are correct. The explicit deny blocks the prohibited production actions even when an applicable policy allows them. Least-privilege cleanup removes unnecessary grants and paths to a different, unrestricted identity. The protected tag and the policies enforcing the restriction must not be editable by developers.

<<3>> verifies possession of an additional authentication factor but still authorizes the wrong people to perform the action. <<4>> changes instance network access, not authorization for EC2 control-plane API calls. <<5>> remains too broad: PowerUserAccess permits EC2 actions, including stopping and terminating instances.

An explicit deny takes precedence over an allow in the applicable policy evaluation. Removing overlapping allows is therefore a complementary least-privilege measure, not a prerequisite for that deny to work. Evaluate the identity the developer can actually use, including role-assumption and policy-editing paths.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic_policy-eval-denyallow.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/PowerUserAccess.html

diagram_alt: Production-tag matching activates an explicit deny that an overlapping allow cannot override, provided developers cannot remove or bypass the controls.

sources.supports: An applicable explicit deny overrides an allow during authorization.
The managed policy permits EC2 actions and does not enforce the requested separation of duties.

editorial_notes: Made the two selected actions explicitly complementary and removed the implication that broad allows override an applicable explicit deny.
Retained tag and privilege-escalation protections that prevent a superficial tag-only control.
